title: Hedge trimming and shaping
audience: Garden maintenance workers and crew leaders who trim, shape and renovate hedges, and who quote and price hedge work.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish a hedge, which is trimmed and shaped as a row of shrubs, from a tree, which is excluded when above a set height or near power lines.
Trim and shape a hedge to a level and line that suits the species, the site and the client's approved scope.
Identify when a hedge renovation needs more time, equipment or a different method, and price it accordingly.
Apply the stop conditions that apply to hedge work at height, near power lines and near services.

instruction.heading: Hedge or tree: where the line sits
instruction.body: Hedge trimming is one of the most common garden jobs and one of the easiest to take too far. A hedge is a planted row of shrubs or small trees that is kept at a managed height and width. A tree is a single plant, usually with a main trunk, that is allowed to grow to its natural height. The line between them is not always clear. A tall cypress that has been planted as a screen, a row of old trees that has been left to grow, or a hedge that has become a canopy can each be treated as a tree in the scope. Before cutting, agree in writing whether the planting is a hedge and what height and width the client expects. Whether a tree needs a council permit depends on the council. One NSW council exempts trees under five metres from its permit rule, but other conditions still apply (no date shown). Brisbane City Council requires a permit ahead of working on protected vegetation that is not exempt (no date shown). Tree work near power lines is excluded from this business. Where a planting may need council approval, or the work would bring tools or people near a line, record the exclusion, tell the client and refer the work to a licensed arborist.

instruction.heading: Planning the cut
instruction.body: Before cutting, look at the hedge as a whole. Note the species, the growth habit, the age and the condition. Check the base for dead wood, gaps and any sign of disease or pests. Check the ground for slopes, steps, services and any irrigation pipes that can be damaged. Decide the target height and width and mark them with a string line or stakes. Most hedges are shaped with a wider base than top so that light reaches the lower growth. Check the agreed scope for any part of the hedge that is excluded, such as the section above a fence or a plant the client wants left alone. Plan the access so that the operator can reach the full length without standing on unstable ground or on a structure. If the hedge needs a ladder or a platform to reach the top, check whether that work is inside the business's authorised access method. If it is not, the work is outside the scope and must be referred.

instruction.heading: Trimming and shaping technique
instruction.body: Trim in an even, controlled pattern. Work from the bottom up on the sides and from one end to the other along the top. Keep the blade moving in a steady sweep and avoid stabbing into dense growth, which can damage the blade and the hedge. Use the string line to check the height and the width at regular intervals, not just at the start and end. Cut back to a healthy lateral or a bud where possible rather than leaving stubs. Avoid cutting a hedge back into bare, leafless wood on one side unless the species can regrow from that point, because it may not recover. If a hedge needs renovation, plan the work over more than one season and tell the client. Clean up the trimmings as you go so that people do not trip over them and so the site stays safe. Check the cut edges and surfaces, and remove any leaves and clippings from the footpath and the drain.

instruction.heading: Equipment, safety and stop conditions
instruction.body: Powered hedge trimmers are electrical or battery tools with sharp reciprocating blades. Check the cord or battery, the blade guard, the handle grip and the blade condition before use, and keep the cord clear of the blade. Keep the blade away from people, pets and fences, and do not cut while anyone is in the cutting arc. Stop work when the blade contacts wire, metal, a stone or a service, when the hedge is above the height that the authorised access method allows, when the operator loses balance or footing, or when a line or service is near the cut. Do not reach over or through the hedge to cut the far side. Walk around, or move the ladder or platform if it is an authorised method. Hearing and eye protection are required for powered trimming, and gloves should resist cuts and sap.

instruction.heading: Pricing and quoting higher-value hedge work
instruction.body: Hedge work is a higher-value service when it is priced for what it involves, not for the time it takes to cut. Factors to price include the length and height of the hedge, the species and its growth rate, the condition of the base, the need for renovation rather than routine trimming, the access method, the waste to be removed, the risk controls needed, and any excluded areas that the client wants reviewed by another contractor. Quote a renovation separately from routine trimming so that the client understands the difference. Record the quote, the scope, the exclusions and any conditions, and get written approval before starting. Do not promise a result, such as the hedge growing back in a set period. Use the business's pricing method, shown in {{business:pricing.pricing_method}}, and do not quote a price that is not approved for the business.

instruction.heading: Verification and escalation
instruction.body: A supervisor should check the line, the shape and the safety. A competent worker can show the target height and width with the string line, explain the difference between a hedge and an excluded tree, describe how they would handle a planting above the authorised height, and describe the stop conditions. Escalate any planting that is above the excluded height, any work that would bring people or tools near a power line, and any renovation that is larger than the approved scope.

procedure: Confirm in writing that the planting is a hedge and that it is within the scope, not a tree above the excluded height.
Check the hedge's species, condition, base growth and ground hazards, including services and irrigation.
Confirm the access method and check that it is authorised for the height of the hedge.
Set the target height and width with a string line or stakes, and mark any excluded section.
Trim from the bottom up on the sides and along the top, keeping the blade moving in controlled sweeps.
Check the string line at intervals and make even cuts to healthy growth.
Clear clippings as you go and keep the footpath, drain and access route clear.
Record the scope, the cut, the exclusions, the waste and the client sign-off, and refer any excluded or larger work in writing.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks for a hedge of mature trees along the side fence to be trimmed to a line. The top is above the fence and the cut would reach close to an overhead service line.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is this hedge work inside the business's scope, and what is the decision?
workedExamples.reasoning: Because the planting is a row of trees that has grown above a set height and the work would take tools near an overhead line, it is excluded from the business. Record the exclusion, explain to the client that the work needs a licensed arborist and that the line is an electrical hazard, and do not start any part of the work. The lower hedge, if it is clearly separate and within the authorised access, can be scoped separately after the client agrees the boundary in writing.

workedExamples.situation: A client wants a hedge that has grown to two metres wide brought back to a neat width of 60 centimetres in one visit.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you scope and quote the job?
workedExamples.reasoning: A hard cut back to a narrow width is a renovation, not a routine trim. Explain that cutting into bare wood may not regrow on some species and that the work may need to be spread over more than one season. Quote the renovation separately with the waste, access and risk controls included, and get written approval. Do not promise the hedge will regrow to a set density.

equipmentAndPpe: Powered hedge trimmer or hand shears, inspected before use
String line and stakes for setting height and width
Eye protection and hearing protection for powered trimming
Access equipment that the business is authorised to use, inspected before use

commonErrors.error: Cutting a hedge that is actually a row of trees without checking the excluded height.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm in writing what the planting is and whether it is above the excluded height before cutting.

commonErrors.error: Cutting a renovation hedge back into bare wood in one visit and damaging the plants.
commonErrors.prevention: Explain the renovation option, quote it separately and plan the work over the right number of seasons.

commonErrors.error: Standing on a ladder or platform beyond the authorised access method to reach the top.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the access method before starting. If it is not authorised for the height, refer the work.

commonErrors.error: Pricing hedge work by the time to cut rather than by the scope and conditions.
commonErrors.prevention: Price the length, height, species, condition, access, waste and renovation level, and record the quote.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Tree work near power lines is excluded from this business. Whether a tree needs a council permit depends on that council's rules.
This lesson does not grant a tree-work licence, an arborist licence or authority to work near power lines.

Overhead power lines are a serious electrocution hazard. The 2014 Safe Work Australia guide describes a no-go zone that people may not enter without the electricity supply authority's written approval, and it allows an authorised person to work in a reduced zone under a risk assessment.
Powered hedge trimmers fall under the model WHS duty to manage plant risks, to the level that is reasonably practicable. Guarding, inspection and safe cutting practice are part of that work.

qualityStandard: The planting is confirmed as a hedge within scope, with any excluded section recorded.
The target height and width are set with a string line and checked at intervals during the cut.
No growth above the authorised access method has been cut, and no work has been done near a power line.
Clippings are cleared from the footpath, drain and access route, and the client has signed the completed work.
documentationEvidence: Hedge scope record with the species, the target height and width, and the excluded sections.
Photographs before and after the work, taken with consent.
Quote and written approval for routine trimming or renovation, with the exclusions listed.
Exclusion and referral record for any planting above the authorised height or near a power line.
summary: A hedge is a managed row of shrubs.
Set the target line with a string and trim evenly from the bottom up.
Renovation is a separate quote and a multi-season plan, not a one-visit cut to bare wood.
Price the scope and conditions, and record the exclusions in writing.

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks for a mature planting along a fence to be cut back. It is above the excluded height and the cut would come close to an overhead line. What is the correct decision?
options: Trim it carefully, since the crew has done hedges of this kind before and knows the height well
Cut the top only and leave the lower part for the crew to finish later on the same day in the afternoon
Record the exclusion, explain the referral to a licensed arborist and do not start any part of the work.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the best approach to a hedge that has grown very wide and needs to be reduced sharply?
options: Treat it as a renovation, quote it separately and plan the work across the seasons the species needs.
Cut it to the target width in one visit, so the client is satisfied immediately.
Cut the far side back to bare wood and leave the client to cope with the result.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which access method is appropriate when the top of a hedge is out of reach from the ground?
options: Any ladder the crew has in the van, since the job is quick and the ladder is close at hand
Only an access method the business is authorised to use for that height, otherwise refer the work.
A chair or stool placed on the hedge base, which is stable enough for a short job on the day
